heldReason.note: The dictionary opens 戶 with a long bar — the 戸 form — where every licensed corpus draws a short dot: 57 units of width against 13 in 扆, and the same difference in 牖. That is a different stroke, not a different direction or order, so both glyphs fail closed and stay out of the runtime and out of later queues until a source carrying the dictionary form exists. Same treatment as 賣's 四·罒, 靑·青 and 兪's 巜·刂 in the earlier grades.

corpusOverrides.note: Four started from Ja and one from MM. 喟 → MM and 劓 → Hans came out clean (two strokes over 60° each to none over 23° and 14°). 贏-style savings again: 鮪 → MM cut four flagged strokes to two and 帷 → Hans three to one. 夤 → Hans removed its single flag. selection.json records every starting corpus and reason.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: 喟, 劓 and 夤 disappeared when the corpus changed. 濰, 黝, 鮪 and 囿 were resolved by reordering and 耰, 濰, 帷 and 軔 by an authored path. 扆 1 (141°) and 牖 5·6·8 turned out to be the 戶 form difference and were held. The endpoint assignment check added the 糸 pair in 濰 and proposed two swaps in 窬 and 异 whose gains were 0.8 and 3.4 — noise, left alone. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 5 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: Short opening dots and inner marks the dictionary draws vertically or steeper than the licensed corpora (窬 1 at 50° and 12 at 48°, 夤 4 at 60°, 袵 1 at 47°, 衽 1 at 48°). Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches.

sourceTransform.note: One dictionary group carries a horizontal offset, translate(12, -830), as in each batch since 厲 in batch 4. serve.py, source-checks.mjs and direction-probe.mjs accept translate(x, -y), and the published paths come from the licensed corpus, so the offset only affects what the review sheet draws.
